pairs.evidence: packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/no-hardcoded-display-string.test.mjs:170 The only invalid case testing a plain hatch uses an unrelated comment, and no suite has an invalid case for a marker with no reason, so `// reduced-motion-ok`, `raw-format-ok`, `i18n-ok` and `citation-ok` all silence their rule with no stated invariant (measured with the real rules through ESLint's Linter: bare and empty-colon markers each returned zero messages) and the suite stays green.

techniques.evidence: packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/no-hardcoded-display-string.test.mjs:170 Property 4 (the written fact at each use) is unpinned for all four plain markers, although the docs say the annotation requires a reason. The structured citation-ok form IS well pinned (require-source-citation.test.mjs lines 228-250). If these markers are classed as suppressions instead, the technique says both share the reason requirement, so the verdict holds.

packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:111 Identity, not behavioural similarity, proves each shim is the package rule, so there is one implementation behind both doors. Suites exercise rules through ESLint's real harness with no hand-written doubles.

pairs.registryProposal: marked-unverifiable-region separates an unverifiable region from a suppression, but a lint annotation can be both: `citation-ok` covers a fact the checker cannot see across a file boundary while also silencing a report. The technique could state which discipline governs that hybrid, and that the reason requirement should be enforced and tested by the checker that accepts the marker, not only documented.
